title: Troponin & the Universal Definition: Above, Moving, Ischaemic
summary: Interpret high-sensitivity troponin with sex-specific 99th percentile limits, separate acute from chronic myocardial injury, apply the 2026 Fifth Universal Definition of MI, and recognise non-ischaemic and analytical causes of a raised result.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 19 Hit 1 (troponin, 99th percentile, rise/fall), Hit 3 (hs-cTn in healthy people; sex-specific limits), Hit 4 (acute vs chronic), Hit 7 (non-MI causes), Hit 8 (biotin/heterophile interference), Trap 5 and the Figure 19 anchor. Checked against Mills 2026 (Fifth UDMI), Domienik-Karłowicz 2021 and Mair 2026. Updated from the reviewer’s Fourth UDMI to the 2026 Fifth UDMI (register flag rv-udmi-fifth). Not taught: numeric ng/L thresholds, type 4a/5 multiples, reinfarction 20% rule, natriuretic peptides, hs-CRP, D-dimer.

objectives: Explain the 99th percentile URL and why sex-specific limits are used.
Distinguish acute from chronic myocardial injury.
Define MI under the 2026 Fifth Universal Definition and name its three clinical types.
Recognise non-ischaemic and analytical causes of raised troponin.

scenes.title: Troponin high — heart attack?
scenes.altText: Three patient cards with high troponin: a marathon runner after a race; a dialysis patient with a stable mildly high value; a woman with chest pain whose value is above the female but below the old unisex cutoff. Question token: “Which of these is a myocardial infarction?”

cues.text: Three people have a raised troponin. A marathon runner, just after the race.
A dialysis patient whose value is always a little high. And a woman with chest pain whose result is above the female cut-off but below the old one-size-fits-all limit.
Troponin tells you the heart is injured — not why. Which of these is a heart attack?

scenes.title: Normal: troponin in healthy people
scenes.altText: A heart-muscle card with troponin tokens inside the sarcomere. High-sensitivity assays detect a small amount of troponin in most healthy people (normal turnover). A reference-population card states that the upper reference limit (URL) is the 99th percentile of healthy people, with a red line marking it. Two markers appear: one for women (lower) and one for men (higher) — sex-specific URLs.

cues.text: Cardiac troponin I and T are part of the heart muscle’s contractile machinery, so they’re specific to heart muscle.
High-sensitivity assays can detect small amounts of troponin in most healthy people — a sign of normal turnover, not disease.
The upper limit of normal is the 99th percentile of a healthy reference population.
Women’s upper limits are lower than men’s for most assays. The 2026 Universal Definition requires sex-specific limits, so injury in women isn’t missed.

scenes.title: What changes: injury, acute or chronic — and infarction
scenes.altText: Three panels of troponin-over-time graphs (schematic bars). Acute myocardial injury: a rise and/or fall with at least one value above the sex-specific 99th percentile URL. Chronic myocardial injury: two or more stable values above the URL in a stable setting (e.g., kidney disease — halving eGFR roughly doubles the baseline). Myocardial infarction: acute injury caused by ischaemia, classified in 2026 as primary (spontaneous acute coronary pathology), secondary (supply–demand imbalance from another acute condition) or procedure-related.

cues.text: Acute myocardial injury means a rise and/or fall in troponin, with at least one value above the sex-specific 99th percentile.
Chronic myocardial injury means two or more values above the limit, but stable, in a stable patient — for example in kidney disease, where halving kidney function roughly doubles the baseline.
A myocardial infarction is acute myocardial injury caused by ischaemia. Injury alone isn’t enough.
The 2026 Fifth Universal Definition replaced the old numbered types with three: primary, secondary, and procedure-related myocardial infarction.

props.title: Fifth UDMI (2026): three clinical types
lines: Secondary — supply–demand imbalance from another acute condition
Procedure-related — complication of a cardiac procedure (≤ 30 days)

scenes.title: In the lab: when troponin misleads
scenes.altText: Non-ischaemic causes of acute injury: acute heart failure, symptomatic atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute brain injury. Exercise: release after strenuous exercise usually stays below 3× URL, peaks hours later and normalises within 48–72 h. Analytical interference: haemolysis and biotin can lower troponin; fibrin micro-clots can raise it; heterophilic antibodies are an uncommon cause of false positives; macrotroponin (troponin–immunoglobulin complexes) gives persistently high values without injury. Action: if a result doesn’t fit the clinical picture, repeat on a new sample and consider interference.

cues.text: Many acute conditions injure the heart without a heart attack: heart failure, fast atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism and acute brain injury.
After hard exercise, troponin may rise — usually less than three times the limit, peaking hours later and normal again within two to three days.
The test itself can mislead. Hemolysis and biotin can push troponin down; fibrin micro-clots can push it up. Heterophilic antibodies occasionally cause false positives.
And macrotroponin — troponin bound to immunoglobulin — clears slowly and stays high without any injury. If a result doesn’t fit the patient, repeat it on a new sample.

props.label: Doesn’t fit? Repeat on a new sample

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Trap card: “High troponin = myocardial infarction” is crossed out → “Troponin shows injury; MI needs acute injury + ischaemia.” Trap card: “A stable raised troponin in kidney disease = acute MI” is crossed out → “No rise/fall = chronic injury.” Trap card: “One unisex cut-off for everyone” is crossed out → “2026: sex-specific 99th percentile URLs.”

cues.text: Trap one: a high troponin isn’t automatically a heart attack. It shows injury; infarction needs acute injury caused by ischaemia.
Trap two: a stable, raised troponin in kidney disease is chronic injury, not an acute infarction — look for the rise or fall.
Trap three: a single unisex cut-off misses injury in women. The 2026 definition uses sex-specific limits.

props.title: ✗ “High troponin = myocardial infarction.”
lines: ✓ Injury; MI needs acute injury + ischaemia

props.title: ✗ “Stable high troponin in CKD = acute MI.”

scenes.title: Above, moving, ischaemic
scenes.altText: Memory aid: an MI needs troponin that is “Above (the sex-specific 99th), Moving (rise/fall), and Ischaemic (clinical cause).” A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: an infarction needs troponin that is above the limit, moving up or down, and ischaemic in cause. Above, moving, ischaemic.

Where it breaks: a very early sample may not yet be above or moving; analytical interference can fake “above”; delta thresholds are assay-specific; and a result is only as good as the sample and the assay.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Acute injury = rise/fall + ≥ 1 value > sex-specific 99th URL · MI = acute injury + ischaemia (primary / secondary / procedure-related)”, “Chronic = stable elevation · interference: biotin/haemolysis ↓, micro-clots ↑, macrotroponin”.

cues.text: Troponin above the sex-specific 99th percentile shows injury; a rise or fall makes it acute; only ischaemia makes it an infarction — and always consider interference when the result doesn’t fit.

props.label: Acute injury: rise/fall + > sex-specific 99th · MI = + ischaemia
Chronic = stable high · biotin/hemolysis ↓ · micro-clots ↑ · macrotroponin

explanation.what: Plain language: troponin tells you heart muscle is injured; its pattern over time tells you whether the injury is new; only an ischaemic cause makes it a heart attack. Scientific terms: acute myocardial injury = rise and/or fall of cTnI/T with ≥ 1 value > sex-specific 99th percentile URL; chronic = ≥ 2 stable values above the URL in a stable setting; MI = acute injury due to ischaemia, classified (Fifth UDMI, 2026) as primary, secondary or procedure-related.
explanation.why: Troponin is cardiac-specific but released by any myocardial injury. High-sensitivity assays detect troponin in most healthy people; women’s URLs are lower. Reduced eGFR raises baseline troponin.
explanation.measure: Serial hs-cTn to detect a delta; sex-specific URLs; repeat unexpected results on a new sample. Interference: haemolysis and biotin can lower, fibrin micro-clots can raise; heterophilic antibodies uncommon false positives; macrotroponin persistently high.
explanation.differs: Acute vs chronic injury (delta vs stable); injury vs infarction (ischaemia); primary vs secondary vs procedure-related MI.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: “is it MI?”, rise/fall interpretation, CKD and exercise troponin, interferences, and (newer) sex-specific limits and Fifth UDMI terminology.

mnemonic.explanation: Above the sex-specific 99th percentile, rising or falling, and caused by ischaemia = myocardial infarction.
mnemonic.limitation: Very early samples may not yet be above or moving; interference can fake “above”; deltas are assay-specific; results depend on sample and assay.

analogyLimitations: Bars and curves are schematic, not assay data.
Accelerated rule-out protocols, natriuretic peptides and D-dimer are not covered here.
takeaway: Troponin above the sex-specific 99th percentile shows injury; a rise or fall makes it acute; only ischaemia makes it an infarction — and always consider interference when the result doesn’t fit.

questions.stem: A patient on haemodialysis has hs-cTnT values of 48, 50 and 49 ng/L over 6 hours (URL 14 ng/L) with no chest pain or ECG changes. Best interpretation?

options.rationale: Correct. Stable values above the URL without a rise/fall indicate chronic injury.
Incorrect. There is no rise/fall and no ischaemia.

options.text: Normal for dialysis, so no injury
options.rationale: Incorrect. Values above the URL still define (chronic) myocardial injury.
Incorrect. Reduced kidney function commonly raises baseline troponin.

questions.stem: Under the Fifth Universal Definition (2026), how is an MI caused by severe anaemia-related supply–demand imbalance in a patient with stable coronary disease classified?

options.rationale: Correct. Ischaemia results from another acute condition causing supply–demand imbalance.
Incorrect. Primary MI is due to acute coronary pathology such as atherothrombosis.
Incorrect. No cardiac procedure was involved.
Incorrect. Ischaemic acute injury is infarction, not chronic injury.

questions.stem: A patient taking high-dose biotin has chest pain and a troponin result below the URL, which seems inconsistent with the ECG. What is the best laboratory response?

options.text: Suspect biotin interference (falsely low result) and repeat/use an unaffected method
options.rationale: Correct. Biotin can reduce troponin results in some immunoassays.
Incorrect. A result inconsistent with the clinical picture should prompt a check for interference.

options.text: Suspect heterophile antibodies raising the result
options.rationale: Incorrect. The result is low, and heterophiles usually cause false positives.
Incorrect. Macrotroponin causes persistently high, not low, values.

references.usedFor: Acute injury: rise/fall with ≥ 1 value above sex-specific 99th percentile URL; chronic injury: ≥ 2 values above URL in a stable setting; sex-specific URLs to avoid under-recognition in women; numerical MI types replaced by primary, secondary and procedure-related MI (≤ 30 days); halving eGFR roughly doubles basal troponin; haemolysis and biotin reduce, fibrin micro-clots increase cTn; heterophilic antibodies uncommon cause of false positives; macrotroponin slowly cleared; repeat unexpected results on a new sample.

references.usedFor: Fourth UDMI: acute injury = cTn above 99th percentile URL with rise/fall; without rise/fall = chronic injury; causes include anaemia, tachyarrhythmia, heart failure, kidney disease, shock, hypoxaemia.

references.citation: Mair J. Clinical gray zones of cardiac troponin interpretation in the emergency department: when increased concentrations do not equal acute coronary syndrome. J Clin Med. 2026;15(12):4444.
references.usedFor: hs-cTn detectable in > 50% of healthy people; URLs differ markedly by sex; causes of acute non-AMI injury (heart failure, AF, pulmonary embolism, acute brain injury); exercise-induced cTn usually < 3 × URL, peaks hours later, normalises within 48–72 h; kidney disease raises cTn.

claims.text: Acute injury: rise/fall + ≥ 1 value > sex-specific 99th URL; chronic: ≥ 2 stable values above URL; MI = acute ischaemic injury.
Fifth UDMI (2026): primary, secondary, procedure-related MI replace numbered types.
hs-cTn detectable in most healthy people; sex-specific URLs.
Non-ischaemic injury: HF, AF, PE, brain injury; exercise < 3 × URL, normal in 48–72 h; reduced eGFR raises baseline.
Haemolysis and biotin lower; micro-clots raise; heterophile uncommon false +; macrotroponin persistently high; repeat on new sample.
Sepsis as a cause of acute myocardial injury.
